description.narrative: Stöd till civilsamhällesorganisation som arbetar i Mekongregionen för att stärka lokala samhällens mänskliga rättigheter, skydd för miljön och verka för klimaträttvisa.
Support to NGO supporting local communities in the Mekong region to protect their human rights, the Environment and request accountability for the climate crisis.

The objective of the intervention is to contribute to the implementation of EarthRights Mekong Regional Program, which is aligned to contribute to the realisation of EarthRight's global strategic plan 2020-2024.
The Regional goals and objectives of the Mekong Regional Program are:
Regional goal 1 - Climate Justice and Accountability
Regional goal 2 - Earth Rights Defenders
Regional Goal 3 - Corporate Accountability
The program is also intended, to the extent relevant for the Mekong Regional Program, to contribute to four of EarthRights six Global Operational Goals:
1. Gender Justice and Social Inclusion.
2. Development and implementation of Physical and Cyber Security Protection
3. Development of an organisational monitoring and evaluation system that will include annual planning, data collection and learning processes to inform program design and goal-setting.
4. Increased policy and research capacity through development of human and financial resources and partnerships

CLIMATE JUSTICE AND ACCOUNTABILITY
- Strengthened national and regional-level climate justice coalition building and advocacy by supporting the Thai Climate Change Action Network and the Cambodia Climate Justice Working Group.
EarthRights convened and trained Cambodian CSOs on climate change law and policy and facilitated the establishment of the Cambodia Climate Justice Working Group in 2023 to co-host joint activities on national-level climate issues. EarthRights International was appointed to be the main facilitator of the network. In Thailand the Climate Change Action Network was established in 2021. During the Thai CCAN exchange visit with Cambodia Climate Change Working Group, CSOs shared what has been learned in addressing climate justice and energy transition issues. Knowledge and information sharing among CSOs and communities is indicative of growth in a coordinated movement. Along with other partners, the Thai CCAN conducted a people's COP where civil society representatives complied policy recommendations to submit to government agencies attending COP 28.
- Thai communities in one coastal area drafted their own community action plan and mechanism/tool for collecting long term community data on the impacts associated with liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal project. This will allow the community to ground legal and campaign efforts on verified evidence of LNG effects in their communities.
EARTH RIGHTS DEFENDERS (ERD)
- Conducted training and produced capacity-building materials on physical, digital, legal, and administrative security for ERDs, including a safety and security manual for ERDs in Southeast Asia and an electronic manual on criminalization and judicial harassment of ERDs in Thai. - Hosted a four-and-a-half-month hybrid EarthRights School session, which 13 students attended from Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.
- Developed an e-learning course that allows students in remote environments and with unstable internet connection to learn in their own pace. Support materials were translated into Mekong languages.
ALUMNI PROGRAM
As of 2023, EarthRights has an extensive network of alumni from their Mekong training programs, including EarthRights School in Myanmar and Thailand, Mekong Legal Advocacy Institute (MLAI), legal fellowships, and other short training programs. During 2023 EarthRights;
- Strengthened connections with alumni from Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Thailand, and Myanmar through in-country gatherings. - Provided funding and mentorship to alumni through the 2023 Alumni Small Grants Program and one-time event sponsorships. - Conducted refresher trainings, including a six-week online project cycle management training and a training on the foundations of online facilitation. - Hosted a Regional Alumni Learning Event aimed at fostering meaningful engagement with alumni. This enabled alumni to facilitate connections and build trust, provide updates on their work, learn about funding opportunities, and exchange experiences and insights on community mobilization efforts.
CORPORATE ACCOUNTABILITY
- Provided targeted support to project-affected communities in the Mekong region to ensure that they have the knowledge, skills, and networks to safely access information on development projects; engage with corporations, international financial institutions, or governments to prevent or mitigate harms; and access remedy for harms.
- Assisted two communities with legal cases: one regarding a proposed coal mine, and one regarding a Water Diversion Project.
- EarthRights strengthened the knowledge, skills, and networks of public interest lawyers to support communities affected by harmful development projects.
- EarthRights built out their Local, Engagement, Action, and Dialogue (LEAD) toolkit and trained community leaders in guiding communities in using the LEAD tools, and directly supported communities in implementing LEAD tools and piloting.
- Increased the research and policy advocacy capacity by carrying out research on climate related laws and policies in Myanmar and Cambodia, performing an informal analysis of key sections of the Cambodian environmental code, conducting research related to their advocacy on gas revenue flows to Myanmar, and producing a report on Enhancing the Role of Environmental Public Interest Litigation to Advance Environmental Rights in Southeast Asia.
- EarthRights is a member of the Extraterritorial Watch Coalition (ETO Watch), a network focusing on the impacts of Thai investments abroad. In 2023, EarthRights worked with ETO Watch to support communities affected by a coal-fired power plant in Laos. The communities were supported in submitting a complaint to the National Human Rights Commission of Thailand.
